core.title: Do not build the derived documentation graph on the pre-existing node-fabricating graph substrate
core.given: The resolver of the derived documentation graph.
core.when: You plan what the resolver builds on.
core.then: The resolver MUST NOT reuse the repository's pre-existing node-fabricating graph-building substrate (the substrate identified by the realization).
avoid: Reusing the repository's pre-existing node-fabricating graph-building substrate. It is the substrate that lacks the no-fabrication discipline.
core.why: That substrate lacks the no-fabrication discipline: it fabricates nodes, synthesizing a node for any target that no artifact declares, so a graph built on it shows unresolved references as resolved instead of reporting them.
evidence: The component that owns the derived documentation graph does not import the pre-existing node-fabricating substrate directly.
verification: Strict disposition: severity 1; every finding fails the check, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

A validator checks that the derived-graph resolver does not reuse the identified substrate: the component that owns the derived documentation graph must not import the substrate directly, and the resolver must not build on it in any other way; each such reuse is a finding. An indirect, incidental dependency elsewhere in that component — one the resolver does not build on — is not by itself a finding.
Detecting the owning component's direct import of the substrate needs an observer the realization must provide (the realization marks the import-detection observer as not yet present).
The check scopes only what the derived-graph resolver builds on; work on the pre-existing traceability graph itself is out of scope.

fires: A plan proposes building the derived documentation graph on top of the repository's pre-existing node-fabricating graph substrate.
doesNotFire: Work on the pre-existing traceability graph itself, not on the derived documentation graph.

neutralityNotes: This rule forbids reuse of one repository-internal artifact, not a stack mechanism, so the core names the artifact only by role — 'the repository's pre-existing node-fabricating graph-building substrate' — and the realization pins its identity (src/atdd/coach/utils/graph/graph_builder.py, its _ensure_node/add_edge fabrication API, the docs extension as the owning component, the validator ref docs_capability) in bunOnly. The Bun title's concrete module name likewise remains only in bun.json. No profile key is proposed: the substrate's identity is rule-specific realization data, not stack structure (vocabulary notProfileKeys), and the core needs no other concrete fact (role, root, suffix, idiom, enforcement) that the closed vocabulary lacks, so profileRequirements is empty. The verification scope is deliberately no broader than bun.json: the check targets resolver reuse of the substrate and the owning component's direct imports (bun.json's evidence is exactly 'the docs extension does not import graph_builder.py'); an indirect, incidental dependency elsewhere in that component, one the resolver does not build on, is not a finding. Instantiating the core's definite reference ('the substrate identified by the realization') with the bunOnly pin yields exactly bun.json's obligation — no exceptions were dropped (unless is empty) and none were added.
